strategy: Add closed structured effect implementations underneath the existing Provider Adapter contracts. A transactional local.workspace adapter will validate path and content-digest preconditions before mutation. A subprocess-based local Git host will create a commit only from an exact parent and exact changed-path set. A GitHub REST host will create a PR and re-read it to prove repository, branches, and exact head SHA. A thin Starter Provider bootstrap will assemble these with existing local process and event-driven CI adapters without creating new capability or write authorities.

changes.responsibility: execute one exact structured workspace mutation transaction with traversal, symlink, digest, scope, rollback, and receipt checks
changes.reason: local.workspace is registered but currently has no executable Provider Adapter

changes.responsibility: publish the strict host-independent workspace mutation request contract
changes.reason: Hosts and generated Workflows need a reviewable non-shell write shape

changes.responsibility: implement real local Git commit and GitHub PR-create hosts behind existing publication adapters
changes.reason: current publication hosts are Protocol-only and tested with fakes

changes.responsibility: assemble local.workspace, local.process, local.git, selected code-review, and selected CI adapters from explicit configuration
changes.reason: installed Starter embeddings should not duplicate security-sensitive registry assembly

changes.responsibility: prove transactional mutation and traversal, symlink, stale digest, duplicate path, out-of-scope, and rollback counterexamples
changes.reason: workspace mutation must fail closed before partial source drift

changes.responsibility: prove a real temporary Git commit and exact GitHub PR request/verification contract with a transport boundary
changes.reason: fake Provider receipts cannot certify concrete effect semantics

changes.responsibility: prove exact Provider registry assembly, missing configuration blockers, and no merge capability
changes.reason: the ChatGPT/Codex embedding needs one tested assembly path

changes.responsibility: add an installed Customer Agent publication route regression using the concrete bootstrap boundary
changes.reason: the Starter runtime must consume the new assembly without changing TaskRun completion semantics

changes.responsibility: document effect contracts, Host injection, credentials, evidence, and standalone product boundary
changes.reason: operators need to understand what runs inside Harness and what remains project-owned

changes.responsibility: replace the stale concrete-adapter boundary with the new bootstrap and remaining Host Skill boundary
changes.reason: the runtime architecture record must match executable coverage

unchanged_boundaries: Capability Registry and Resolver remain the sole Provider binding authorities
WorkflowAdapterDispatcher remains the sole graph-step dispatch owner
the existing WriteAuthorityGuard runs before every mutating Provider invocation
a mutating Skill still requires the existing Guard before the real Skill Host edits source
publication_provider_adapters remain the receipt-validation boundary for Git and code review
GitHub credentials authorize the remote API but do not replace repository ChangePermit or WriteAuthorityGuard
Customer Agent Workflows contain no merge step and the bootstrap exposes no automatic merge path
Graph END projects only to TaskRun VALIDATING and never COMPLETED
customer application runtime and dependencies remain independent of Harness
forbidden_repairs: Do not execute shell strings supplied by Workflow or Skill output.
Do not accept absolute paths, traversal, symlinks, missing precondition digests, or undeclared changed paths.
Do not let a workspace request write governance evidence or Harness quality output as product source.
Do not create a Git commit when HEAD differs from expected_parent_sha or the worktree contains out-of-scope changes.
Do not trust the GitHub create response without an exact-head verification read.
Do not log, persist, or return GitHub tokens.
Do not add PR merge to Customer Agent Starter bootstrap.
Do not mark TaskRun complete from adapter, Git, PR, CI, Quality, or Graph END success.
required_invariants: workspace mutations are all-or-rollback and receipt-bind before/after SHA-256 for every path
local Git commit parent and changed paths exactly match the request
GitHub PR receipt is re-read and exact-head bound
Provider assembly requires explicit workspace, profiles, repository, token source, and provider IDs
missing credentials, repository drift, remote mismatch, or transport failure becomes blocked evidence
no concrete adapter acquires completion, quality, merge, or write authority

focused: structured create/replace/delete transaction produces exact digest-bound receipt
real temporary Git repository produces an exact-parent exact-path commit
GitHub PR create request and verification read produce an exact-head receipt
Starter Provider bootstrap registers the activated concrete providers
counterexamples: path traversal, absolute path, symlink, stale digest, duplicate path, protected path, and partial failure are rejected
dirty out-of-scope Git path, wrong parent, empty diff, and receipt path mismatch are rejected
missing token, wrong repository, wrong remote head, invalid PR identity, and transport error are rejected
bootstrap cannot register duplicate providers or enable automatic merge
regression: Dispatcher, publication Provider, Starter runtime, Capability, Workflow, TaskRun, and control-plane suites remain green
negative_path: no shell command from runtime state is executed
no token appears in evidence or exception messages
no static Capability, Workflow, Skill, or Provider registry row is added
Graph END remains VALIDATING and Customer Agent Workflows still have no merge capability

risks: Workspace rollback can fail under concurrent external mutation; the adapter will detect post-write drift, attempt bounded rollback, and block with explicit evidence.
Git hooks may reject a commit; failure remains blocked and no fabricated receipt is emitted.
GitHub response shapes or permissions may vary; the host validates only the required stable contract and blocks otherwise.
ChatGPT/Codex still supplies the real model-driven Skill Host; this change closes deterministic workspace/publication effects, not model execution itself.
rollback_plan: Remove the concrete workspace/publication hosts and Starter Provider bootstrap plus their schemas/tests/docs. The existing injected Protocol adapters and runtime remain intact and continue to fail closed when no embedding host is supplied.
